prompts.1A:
Build a read-only inventory of every managed switch in Catalyst Center.
Resolve the switch family from inventory, retrieve all pages, and exclude APs,
controllers, and routers.

Return a table with hostname, management IP, model, software version, role,
reachability, and uptime where available. Retrieve device details when the list
response lacks a requested field. Sort unreachable devices first.
Include the total examined, retrieval failures, and collection timestamps.
Do not make changes.
prompts.2A:
Perform a read-only port audit on 10.85.134.65. Resolve the device, obtain its
interface count, and retrieve all interface pages.

Return interface name, administrative state, operational state, port mode,
VLAN ID, speed, and duplex where returned. Separate administratively disabled
ports from ports that are enabled but operationally down. Do not assume a down
port is faulty or unused. Include the total examined and any missing pages.
prompts.6B:
Resolve the exact site Global/Vancouver Canada/VNC2. List managed switches assigned directly to that
site, excluding descendant sites for this report. For each switch show hostname,
IP, and assigned site. Report any devices whose assignment lookup fails.
Do not pass a site UUID to a tool that expects a device UUID. Read-only.
prompts.7B:
For 10.85.134.65, show overall compliance and every category actually returned.
Include assessment time and supporting details where available. Separate failed,
warning, not-applicable, and unknown states without changing their meaning.
Explain which findings need investigation; do not infer a remediation action
from the status alone. Do not change anything.
prompts.8A:
Review configuration-compliance remediation for 10.85.134.65.
First resolve the exact device and retrieve its compliance findings. Identify
which findings the remediation API can address and explain the possible network
flap and lack of dry-run. Present the target and proposed action, then STOP and
ask for explicit approval. This request is not approval to execute.

Only after I approve the exact target and action, submit remediation once.
Track its task to a terminal outcome if the available task tools support that
returned task ID. Report success, failure, no-op, or unverified outcome clearly.
Do not resubmit if task tracking fails.

certification_scope: Fresh-agent read-only run supported by Python FastMCP Client; not certification of a different native chat client.
safety: Only discovered GET tools invoked. No configuration retrieval, credentials, direct controller REST, remediation, publication, service changes, or commits.
sanitization: Secret/configuration/diff fields excluded; collection is narrowed to operational inventory, interfaces, assignment, and compliance.
preflight_note: Live schema discovery preceded this harness. One target lookup used api_getNetworkDeviceByIP(ipAddress=10.85.134.65); local result.model_dump introspection failed (AttributeError). No controller error or mutation; no raw response saved. Preflight exact UTC times unavailable. Acceptance calls below have exact UTC times.

remediation_review.description:
Remediates configuration compliance issues. Compliance issues related to 'Routing', 'HA Remediation', 'Software Image', 'Securities Advisories', 'SD-Access Unsupported Configuration', 'Workflow', etc. will not be addressed by this API.

Warning: Fixing compliance mismatches could result in a possible network flap.

category.description: OPTIONAL filter. Leave UNSET unless the user explicitly names a compliance category. Setting it narrows results to that category and HIDES others, so for a general "violations / details" request omit it entirely and NEVER default it to RUNNING_CONFIG. See the COMPLIANCE TYPE & CATEGORY MAPPING in the tool description (category INTENT covers complianceType NETWORK_PROFILE / FABRIC / APPLICATION_VISIBILITY / WORKFLOW). Allowed values: 'INTENT', 'RUNNING_CONFIG', 'IMAGE', 'PSIRT', 'DESIGN_OOD', 'EOX', 'NETWORK_SETTINGS'.

complianceType.description: OPTIONAL filter. Leave UNSET unless the user explicitly names one or more compliance types (comma-separated). Setting it narrows results to those type(s) and HIDES violations of all other types, so for a general "violations / details" request omit it entirely and NEVER default it to RUNNING_CONFIG — the word "config" in a request (e.g. "ACL-config template", "config template") does NOT mean RUNNING_CONFIG; RUNNING_CONFIG is ONLY a startup-vs-running config mismatch. Use the COMPLIANCE TYPE & CATEGORY MAPPING in the tool description to translate the user's wording/sub-type to the correct PARENT type (e.g. CLI/config/feature template -> NETWORK_PROFILE, syslog -> NETWORK_SETTINGS, CBAR -> APPLICATION_VISIBILITY); sub-type names such as CLI_TEMPLATE are NOT valid values. Allowed values: 'APPLICATION_VISIBILITY', 'EOX', 'FABRIC', 'IMAGE', 'NETWORK_PROFILE', 'NETWORK_RULES', 'NETWORK_SETTINGS', 'PSIRT', 'RUNNING_CONFIG', 'WORKFLOW'.

deviceUuid.description: Device UUID. Use the get_device_details tool to retrieve the device UUID if you only have the device name or IP.

diffList.description: OPTIONAL — leave UNSET for general violations/details requests (setting diffList, or a complianceType, can hide other violation types). Set to true ONLY for explicit intended-vs-actual questions. Pass true to fetch the configuration DIFF (the diffList). The default response (diffList omitted or false) does NOT include the intended-versus-configured values, so set diffList=true whenever the user asks what should have been configured vs what is present now, intended vs actual / expected vs current config, a config difference / diff, a side-by-side comparison, what changed, what is missing, or the exact configuration of a specific violation instance (e.g. a telemetry subscription id or a feature). When true, each diffList entry provides an op (add/remove/update) plus the intended value and the configured value; combine with the relevant complianceType to scope the diff. NOTE: diffList does NOT include the actual CLI template (config template) violation content even when true — that content can be huge; for in-depth CLI template violation analysis, recommend Deep Reasoning mode.

remediationSupported.description: OPTIONAL filter ('true' or 'false'). Leave UNSET unless the user explicitly asks to filter by remediation support; when unset, the result includes both remediation-supported and unsupported violations.

status.description: OPTIONAL filter. Leave UNSET unless the user explicitly filters by a compliance status; when unset, violations of all statuses are returned. Allowed values: 'COMPLIANT', 'NON_COMPLIANT', 'ERROR', 'IN_PROGRESS', 'NOT_APPLICABLE', 'NOT_AVAILABLE', 'WARNING', 'REMEDIATION_IN_PROGRESS'.

limit.description: Maximum number of records to be fetched. If not provided, 10 records will be fetched by default

name.description: Site name, including area, building, or floor name.

nameHierarchy.description: Exact full site hierarchy path starting with 'Global/', such as 'Global/AreaName/BuildingName/FloorName'. Prefer this over `name` whenever the user provides or clearly implies the FULL hierarchy.

offset.description: The first record to show for this page. Minimum value is 1

type.description: Site type: area, building, or floor.

family.description: Product family of the network device. For example, Switches, Routers, etc.

limit.description: Maximum number of records to be fetched. If not provided, 500 records will be fetched by default

managementAddress.description: Management address of the network device

managementState.description: The status of the network device's manageability. Available statuses are MANAGED, UNDER_MAINTENANCE, NEVER_MANAGED. Refer features for more details.

offset.description: The first record to show for this page. Minimum value is 1

order.description: Whether ascending or descending order should be used to sort the response.

reachabilityStatus.description: Reachability status of the network device. Available values : REACHABLE, ONLY_PING_REACHABLE, UNREACHABLE, UNKNOWN. Refer features for more details.

role.description: Role assigned to the network device. Available values : BORDER_ROUTER, CORE, DISTRIBUTION, ACCESS, UNKNOWN

serialNumber.description: Serial number of the network device

sortBy.description: A property within the response to sort by. Available values : id, managementAddress, dnsResolvedManagementIpAddress, hostname, macAddress, type, family, series, platformids, softwareType, softwareVersion, vendor, bootTime, role, roleSource, apEthernetMacAddress, apManagerInterfaceIpAddress, apWlcIpAddress, deviceSupportLevel, reachabilityFailureReason, resyncStartTime, resyncEndTime, resyncReasons, pendingResyncRequestCount, pendingResyncRequestReasons, resyncIntervalSource, resyncIntervalMinutes

stackDevice.description: Flag indicating if the device is a stack device

status.description: Inventory related status of the network device. Available values : MANAGED, SYNC_NOT_STARTED, SYNC_INIT_FAILED, SYNC_PRECHECK_FAILED, SYNC_IN_PROGRESS, SYNC_INTERNAL_ERROR, SYNC_DISABLED, DELETING_DEVICE, UNDER_MAINTENANCE, QUARANTINED, UNASSOCIATED, UNREACHABLE, UNKNOWN. Refer features for more details.

views.description: The specific views being requested. This is an optional parameter which can be passed to get one or more of the network device data. If this is not provided, then it will default to BASIC views. If multiple views are provided, the response will contain the union of the views. Refer features for more details. Available values : BASIC, RESYNC, USER_DEFINED_FIELDS.
